During my summer internship at Traycer AI, Inc., I focused on front-end development for the Memories 
feature, utilizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) technology to enhance the user experience in 
Traycer’s AI-powered code analysis tool. Working closely with the engineering team, I developed React 
components to seamlessly display memory-based insights, creating an intuitive and responsive interface. My 
work involved designing interactive UI elements that enabled developers to easily access and manage 
contextual suggestions within their coding environment. This experience strengthened my skills in crafting 
user-friendly interfaces for AI-driven tools, focusing on delivering a smooth, productive experience for 
end-users.

3. Technical Approach 

3.1 Overview of RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) System 
The Memories feature leverages a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to provide contextually 
relevant suggestions within the front-end interface. RAG combines retrieval and generation techniques, 
pulling relevant information from prior interactions or documentation and presenting it in a way that enhances 
the current coding context. This setup enables the front-end to display meaningful, context-aware insights 
directly within the IDE, helping developers quickly access relevant suggestions and improve their workflow 
without switching contexts. The RAG-driven UI elements make the user experience seamless, displaying 
suggestions in real-time and in alignment with the user’s current development focus.
nt focus.

3.2 Development Process 
The development process involved key stages focused on front-end integration and performance optimization: 
initial UI design, embedding the retrieval mechanisms, testing for response accuracy, and optimizing for 
speed. In the interface, Pinecone was integrated as the vector database to efficiently store and retrieve 
embeddings, enabling fast access to relevant memories. OpenAI’s large embedding model generated 
high-context embeddings that seamlessly aligned with the front-end display, ensuring suggestions were highly 
relevant. Additionally, Supabase served as the data storage layer, providing a reliable backend for managing 
retrieval operations and supporting a smooth user experience within the IDE. 

3.3 Challenges and Solutions 
Ensuring a responsive UI with real-time data retrieval was a primary challenge, requiring efficient loading 
indicators and asynchronous data handling to avoid delays. Managing large embeddings from OpenAI while

3.4 Implementation Details 
The RAG system was configured to retrieve the most relevant matches, with Pinecone storing and searching 
vectorized representations of past interactions to support quick access within the UI. Supabase served as the 
primary data store, managing and tracking interactions to maintain memory consistency. Leveraging 
OpenAI’s large embedding model, the system generated embeddings that captured the semantic context of 
past interactions, ensuring that the suggestions displayed in the UI were both meaningful and specific to the 
developer’s current coding context. This configuration provided developers with targeted, context-aware 
insights seamlessly integrated into their IDE.
